title: Prefill/Decode Auctioneer: latency-first fairness allocator for phase slots
creator: Anika Rao
description: Introduce an auction-based allocator ("Auctioneer") for prefill/decode phase slot assignment that balances low-latency requests against overall throughput and tenant fairness. Motivation: existing slot allocators either prioritize throughput (burst consolidation) or enforce strict proportional fairness; neither adapts well to mixed workloads where some requests need sub-100ms tails while others are throughput-optimized.
comments: 2026-02-28 - Anika Rao: Created initial RFC. Auctioneer idea uses per-request bids computed from: estimated entropy (token prediction entropy heuristic), prompt length, KV cache hit probability, tenant QoS credits, and declared latency sensitivity. Bids are continuous scores; allocator runs every scheduling epoch to assign phase slots. Hedging: second-place bidders get soft-hedge tokens to reduce tail when winners slow down.

2026-03-03 - Marco Chen: Implemented prototype in scheduling sandbox (sim cluster). Core modules: bid generator, slot auction loop, moving-average fairness ledger, reserve-price controller. Hooked kernel-hint metadata into auction outputs so we can prefer low-latency kernels for winners.

2026-03-05 - Perf Team (automated): Synthetic mixed workload run (60% background throughput, 40% latency-sensitive): baseline scheduler p95=340ms, auctioneer prototype p95=298ms (12.4% reduction) for latency class; cluster throughput decreased by ~3.1% at same concurrency. CPU/GPU utilization changed: marginally higher short-lived kernel swaps (+5% kernel churn).

2026-03-07 - PM review (Sofia Martinez): Requested clearer safety guardrails for customers on Dedicated (how bids interact with committed capacity) and a user-configurable knob to toggle strict latency-first mode. Also asked for a fail-open fallback to proportional allocation on overload.

2026-03-09 - Design (Luis Ortega): Provided UX copy for Console feature card: 'Latency-first slot allocation' with toggle for 'Weighted fairness' and a small modal explaining entropy-based bids. Asked for an observability surface showing per-tenant bid distribution and hedging events.

2026-03-11 - Marco Chen: Opened draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1489. Added unit tests for bid monotonicity and integration test that validates hedging path when winner stalls. Linked perf dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-internal/r/auctions/mixed-workloads-03-05.

2026-03-12 - Anika Rao: Updated RFC to include acceptance criteria and rollout plan. Added dependency on kernel selection telemetry to evaluate kernel-hinting effectiveness. Noted potential risk: increased kernel switching may increase GPU scheduler overhead; experiment needs to measure driver-level context switch counts.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for latency-tagged requests improves >=10% vs baseline in mixed workload A/B
overall throughput regression <=5% at target concurrency for same cluster size
per-tenant fairness ledger prevents starvation for tenants with non-zero credits over a 1h window
Console shows bid distribution and top-3 winning tenants per epoch
Automatic fallback to proportional allocation under sustained >90% slot contention
next_steps: Finish PR review and merge feature flag behind 'auctioneer_enabled'
Run multi-cluster A/B for 48h on staging with realistic customer traces
Add kernel-switching cost metric to observability (driver context-switch counts, per-kernel latency variance)
Design release notes and Console UX for toggle and explanatory modal
Coordinate with Dedicated product to add explicit tenant reserve-price policy integration
